newsitem.title: USA: Dow finishes flat but retailers, techs shine.
newsitem.headline: Dow finishes flat but retailers, techs shine.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks climbed back from a drop of nearly 50 points to end unchanged Monday as buying of shares likely to benefit from the holiday shopping season overcame nervousness over fresh economic news.
The Nasdaq composite index, heavily weighted with shares of computer makers and other high-technology companies, set its sixth consecutive record, rising 7.21 to 1,299.82.

"Retailers and the usual list of tech suspects are helping us out. Some retailers are saying it was the best Thanksgiving weekend (for Christmas sales) in history," said Michael LaTronica, director of research at Gruntal & Co.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended at 6,521.70, unchanged from Friday, after falling about 49 points earlier in the session. In the broader market, 1,270 stocks rose and 1,200 fell on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 412.5 million shares. The market was closed for Thanksgiving on Thursday and held a shortened session on Friday.

Bond prices fell early in the session on surprisingly strong economic data, which fanned investors' worries about inflation and a possible move by the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates. That pressured stocks in early trading, and the Dow was off more than 30 points for much of the morning.
But as bonds rebounded a bit stocks started roaring back.
"The stronger numbers caused bonds to shake out but it's hard to stop the momentum. There's still the affinity to buy," said Larry Wachtel, a market analyst at Prudential Securities.

The National Association of Purchasing Management said its index of manufacturing rose to 52.7 in November from 50.2 in October, compared with forecasts for 50.8. A reading above 50 signals growth while one below that points to contraction.
Separately, the Commerce Department said construction spending rose 1.8 percent in October, suprising analysts who had forecast that spending dropped.
Analysts said that after the Dow's spectacular 8 percent rise in November, the market was due for a pause.
"It was actually a pretty good day because the focus shifted from blue chips, and gave those a rest, to secondaries and other techs," Wachtel said.

Among retailers gaining after a strong start to the holiday sales season, Sears added 1-1/2 to 51-1/4, Federated Department Stores rose 1-5/8 to 35-3/4, and Gap gained 1-1/4 to 33-3/8. Retailers chalk up a quarter or more of their annual profits over the holidays.
Technology issues also drew buyers, with Micron up 2-5/8 to 35-3/4, Iomega up 2-3/8 to 25 and Western Digital adding 4-3/4 to 58-1/2 after unveiling new products.
Digital Equipment surged 3-1/4 to 40. Salomon upgraded Digital to strong buy from buy.
IBM added 3-7/8 to 163-1/4, a nine-year high. Prudential raised its 12-month price target to $185-$190 from $160.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks fell 0.46 point to 756.56.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.29 point to 398.14. The average share lost 3 cents.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 1.45 to 592.93.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,295.570, up 3.413, or 0.05 percent.
